holidays.name: National Sardines Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the humble, oily little fish that lives in a tin. Fans celebrate by eating sardines on crackers, toast, or straight from the can, while skeptics celebrate by opening a window.
holidays.origin: Like many American food observances, it appears to have been created by food enthusiasts and promoters rather than by any official proclamation. Its exact founder is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Sardines are named after the Italian island of Sardinia, where they were once found in huge numbers.

holidays.name: National Espresso Day
holidays.description: A day for caffeine lovers to toast the tiny, powerful cup of concentrated coffee. Expect jittery enthusiasm, tiny cups, and people saying they only need one shot.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food and drink observance, popularized by coffee fans and cafes. The espresso machine itself was patented in Italy in 1884 by Angelo Moriondo.
holidays.funFact: Despite the common belief, espresso actually has less caffeine per serving than a regular cup of drip coffee, though it is far more concentrated by volume.

holidays.name: Celebrate Your Unique Talent Day
holidays.description: A day for showing off your strange and wonderful skills, whether it is juggling, whistling through your teeth, or folding a fitted sheet. No talent is too odd to be celebrated.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance meant to encourage people to share their gifts with the world rather than hiding them away.
holidays.funFact: Guinness World Records tracks thousands of unusual talents, including the most spoons balanced on a human body.

holidays.name: Evolution Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the science of evolution, marking the anniversary of the publication of Charles Darwin's famous book. Fans of natural selection may be seen proudly wearing shirts with fish growing legs.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the November 24, 1859 publication of On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection. The first printing sold out on its first day.
holidays.funFact: The first print run of 1,250 copies of Darwin's book was reportedly oversubscribed on the very first day it was available to booksellers.

holidays.name: Black Cat Appreciation Day Eve Cuddle Day (Unofficial Cat Lover Observance)
holidays.description: An informal day when cat lovers give extra attention to their feline overlords, especially the sleek black ones who are unfairly accused of being bad luck.
holidays.origin: Rooted in various animal welfare efforts that try to counter superstitions about black cats and boost their adoption rates.
holidays.funFact: Black cats are often adopted less frequently than other cats in shelters, a phenomenon some shelter workers call 'Black Cat Syndrome'.
